frames.label: Engine-to-gearbox swaps typically require a bellhousing adapter plate, and fabricating that plate is straightforward...
frames.main_point: Engine-to-gearbox swaps typically require a bellhousing adapter plate, and fabricating that plate is straightforward with CNC equipment. The adapter itself is not the difficult part of the conversion.
frames.source_quote: A plate between the flywheel housing on the engine and the bell housing of the gearbox would almost certainly be required to mount the gearbox. This would be no problem to produce with a CNC machine.
frames.subject: adapter plate fabrication via CNC
frames.thread_title: Can I use a CNC machine or waterjet to make an adapter plate to adapt a 5 speed transmission to a rare, obsolete engine?

frames.label: Before fitting a different gearbox, verify all critical interfaces and packaging: clutch clearance and actuation, inp...
frames.main_point: Before fitting a different gearbox, verify all critical interfaces and packaging: clutch clearance and actuation, input shaft engagement and spline compatibility, shifter location/clearance, transmission tunnel fit, underbody clearances, crossmember/mount compatibility, and driveshaft alignment, connection/slip, and length.
frames.source_quote: Will the gearbox obstruct the clutch assembly in any way? Will the gearbox imput shaft engage in the clutch? Will the splines of the imput shaft mate and be driven by the clutch? Will the clutch release mechanism operate the clutch successfully? Will the gearshift lever enter the cab? Will the gear shift lever be obstructed in anyway when shifting gear? Will the gearbox casing fit in the transmission tunnel? Will the gearbox effect the underbody position of things like the exhaust system or fuel tank? Will the gearbox cross member accept the new gearbox mountings? Will the propshaft alignment be in alignment? Will the propshaft connect to the gearbox and allow a sliding joint? Will the propshaft length now be too long or too short to connect to the differencial?
frames.subject: transmission swap interface checks
frames.thread_title: Can I use a CNC machine or waterjet to make an adapter plate to adapt a 5 speed transmission to a rare, obsolete engine?

frames.label: Because the vehicle was built around its original drivetrain, reconciling all the mismatches to fit a different gearb...
frames.main_point: Because the vehicle was built around its original drivetrain, reconciling all the mismatches to fit a different gearbox often makes the project uneconomical in time and money. The cumulative integration work can render the swap not viable.
frames.source_quote: When your vehicle was first built it was with its present configuration. You would need to reconcile each every difference from that first build. In time and expense terms it would be highly unlikely to be a viable undertaking.
frames.subject: custom gearbox swap cost viability

frames.label: When adapting an automotive transmission to a non-automotive engine, the solution often includes both an adapter plat...
frames.main_point: When adapting an automotive transmission to a non-automotive engine, the solution often includes both an adapter plate and a flywheel spacer to compensate for required geometry and spacing.
frames.source_quote: They make adapter plates to mate automotive transmissions to non-automotive engines (they also make the spacers for the flywheel to compensate).
frames.subject: flywheel spacer use with transmission adapter plates

frames.label: Prefer purchasing an existing adapter solution for engine-to-transmission mating because it arrives much faster than...
frames.main_point: Prefer purchasing an existing adapter solution for engine-to-transmission mating because it arrives much faster than designing and machining a custom adapter; only consider DIY if cost pressures outweigh time-to-solution.
frames.source_quote: Unless cost is a factor, something already exists to mate your engine to a different tranny, so why try to machine something up your self. Phoenix has what you need and can get it to you a lot faster than you can re-engineer something to fit in.
frames.subject: buy vs build adapter plate decision

frames.label: Evaluate swapping to a different engine/transmission combo as a potential cost-saving alternative to custom adapters,...
frames.main_point: Evaluate swapping to a different engine/transmission combo as a potential cost-saving alternative to custom adapters, as local availability and choices can make a full swap cheaper overall.
frames.source_quote: Consider putting a different engine/tranny combo into your vehicle. Depending on what you might choose, this may actually be a cheaper option, especially considering the area of the States you are located.
